investigation: All three Sky arms exceeded the 8.33 ms interval in this loaded 1440p run, even with capture off. Trace and compose dominate at the same render dimensions, ray count and resource bytes. The broken and overcast traces visited 51% and 4.3% as many samples as fair and spent 116% and 37% as long. The trace counter includes empty visits and excludes nested Sun-path lighting work. Fair rays often visit empty space. Opaque deck rays reach the transmission threshold quickly after sampling dense cloud. The broken weather-map pass rose from 0.137 to 0.239 ms. The map dimensions and declared loops match and the timer does not report row-level occupancy or GPU residency, so the measurement cannot isolate weather values from the cost of the row schedule and concurrent load. The ground-field pass rose from 0.066 to 0.102 and 0.124 ms. The shader issues the same dispatch, with the path texture chosen by tile and no density-dependent work. Hemisphere light rose from 0.054 to 0.073 ms in overcast. Both arms use the same clear-air hemisphere quadrature. Ground and hemisphere work sizes do not explain their timing changes. Resolve rose from 0.272 to 0.425 and 0.540 ms. More opaque fronts may take the history branch in its fixed-size dispatch. This run does not isolate branch cost from shared load. The recent finer-deck trial reported no named-pass increases of 25% at the same view. Keep these work counts, pass times and unmatched load witnesses for later controlled tuning.
estimates: CLOUDS DESIGN cost account: weather <0.1 ms, Sun 0.1–0.2 ms, ground <0.05 ms; profiles and resource bytes recorded separately.
